# 402-mcp: Full Technical Reference

> For a concise overview, see [llms.txt](llms.txt). This document provides the complete technical reference for integrating with, building on, or contributing to 402-mcp.

## What is 402-mcp?

402-mcp is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives AI agents economic agency: the ability to discover, pay for, and consume L402 and other Lightning or ecash payment-gated APIs without human registration, API keys, or middlemen.

It implements the client side of the L402 protocol: when an API responds with HTTP 402 (Payment Required), 402-mcp automatically parses the challenge, pays the Lightning invoice, stores the credential, and retries the request, all within a single tool call from the agent's perspective.

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  AI Agent (Claude, Cursor, GPT, custom)                     │
│  Communicates via MCP protocol (stdio or HTTP transport)     │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                       │ MCP tool calls
┌──────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  402-mcp MCP Server                                          │
│                                                              │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌─────────────┐               │
│  │ Tools    │  │ Wallets  │  │ Stores      │               │
│  │          │  │          │  │             │               │
│  │ config   │  │ NWC      │  │ Credentials │               │
│  │ discover │  │ Cashu    │  │ (AES-256)   │               │
│  │ fetch    │  │ LNURLcash│  │             │               │
│  │ pay      │  │ Human    │  │ Cashu       │               │
│  │ creds    │  │          │  │ Tokens      │               │
│  │ balance  │  │          │  │             │               │
│  │ search   │  │          │  │ LNURLcash   │               │
│  │ buy_cred │  │          │  │ notes       │               │
│  │ redeem   │  │          │  │             │               │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └─────────────┘               │
│                                                              │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐     │
│  │ L402 Protocol│  │ Resilient    │  │ Spend         │     │
│  │ parse, detect│  │ Fetch        │  │ Tracker       │     │
│  │ cache, bolt11│  │ SSRF, retry  │  │ atomic caps   │     │
│  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └───────────────┘     │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                       │ HTTP + L402 / Nostr
         ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
         ▼             ▼             ▼
    ┌─────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐
    │toll-booth│  │ Aperture │  │  Nostr   │
    │ server  │  │  server  │  │  Relays  │
    └─────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘
```

## Source Structure

```
src/
  index.ts                 # Entry point: config, wiring, transport setup
  config.ts                # Environment variable parsing with validation
  spend-tracker.ts         # Atomic rolling-window spend limiter (60s and persisted 24h)
  http-security.ts         # HTTP transport: bearer auth, Host allowlist
  tools/
    config.ts              # l402-config: introspect capabilities
    discover.ts            # l402-discover: probe pricing without paying
    fetch.ts               # l402-fetch: full L402 payment flow
    pay.ts                 # l402-pay: explicit invoice payment
    reconcile.ts           # l402-reconcile: resolve unknown-outcome payments
    store-token.ts         # l402-store-token: store a token from a payment page
    fetch-preview.ts       # l402-fetch-preview: price preview, cannot spend
    credentials.ts         # l402-credentials: list stored credentials
    balance.ts             # l402-balance: check cached credit balance
    search.ts              # l402-search: discover services on Nostr
    buy-credits.ts         # l402-buy-credits: toll-booth credit tiers
    redeem-cashu.ts        # l402-redeem-cashu: direct ecash redemption
    nostr-subscribe.ts     # Nostr relay subscription for search
    storage-discovery.ts   # Validate storage service announcements (Wildbloom) for search
    confirm.ts             # Ask the human directly (MCP elicitation) before an unusual payment
    register-widgets.ts    # MCP Apps widget tools and resources
    untrusted.ts           # Mark third-party text as untrusted content
    safe-error.ts          # Error sanitisation (strips internal details)
    safe-headers.ts        # Header sanitisation (strips auth tokens)
  wallet/
    types.ts               # WalletProvider interface
    resolve.ts             # First-available wallet resolution (NWC, Cashu, LNURLcash, human)
    nwc.ts                 # @forgesworn/nwc-kit adapter + farrier proof check
    cashu.ts               # Cashu ecash melt implementation
    lnurlcash.ts           # LNURLcash bearer-note melt implementation (with lnurlcash-note.ts, lnurlcash-ops.ts)
    human.ts               # Human-in-the-loop (QR code + polling)
  l402/
    parse.ts               # Parse WWW-Authenticate L402 challenges
    detect.ts              # Detect toll-booth vs generic L402 servers
    bolt11.ts              # Decode BOLT11 invoices (amount extraction)
    challenge-cache.ts     # Cache parsed challenges for l402-pay
  x402/
    parse.ts               # Experimental custom x402 format: X-Payment-Required: x402 header, EVM challenge body
    payment.ts             # Format payment request with EIP-681 deeplink for human payment
  xcashu/
    parse.ts               # Detect X-Cashu header; parse NUT-18 payment request
    payment.ts             # Autonomous ecash payment: coin-select, send exact token amount
  xlnurlcash/
    parse.ts               # Detect X-LNURLcash header; parse the lnurlcash payment request
                           # (v/id/amount-as-string/currency/methodDetails.mints, per the
                           #  conformance vectors; the older short form is still read)
    payment.ts             # Autonomous bearer-note payment: pick or split a note to the exact price
  ietf-payment/
    parse.ts               # Detect/parse WWW-Authenticate: Payment challenges (draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01)
    credential.ts          # Build Authorization: Payment base64url credential after Lightning payment
  store/
    credentials.ts         # Encrypted credential persistence (JSON)
    cashu-tokens.ts        # Cashu token store (add/remove/balance)
    lnurlcash-notes.ts     # LNURLcash bearer note store
    pending-payments.ts    # Ledger of unknown-outcome payments
    encryption.ts          # AES-256-GCM encryption (keychain or file key)
  fetch/
    transport.ts           # URL classification (onion/hns/https/http) and selection
    hns-resolve.ts         # Handshake name resolution via DNS-over-HTTPS (RFC 8484)
    resilient-fetch.ts     # Timeout, retry, response size limits, transport fallback
    ssrf-guard.ts          # Block requests to private/internal IPs, HNS fallback
    socks-proxy.ts         # SOCKS5 routing for TOR_PROXY (.onion only) and SOCKS_PROXY (all)
    errors.ts              # Fetch error types (including TransportUnavailableError)
  widgets/                 # MCP Apps widget HTML (built to src/widgets/dist by npm run build)
tests/                     # Mirrors src/ structure
  e2e/                     # Integration tests against in-process toll-booth
```

## Complete Tool Reference

### l402-config

**Purpose:** Introspect the agent's payment capabilities and current configuration.

**Parameters:** None.

**Returns:**
- `nwcConfigured` (boolean): whether an NWC wallet URI is set
- `cashuConfigured` (boolean): whether Cashu tokens are loaded with balance > 0
- `cashuBalanceSats` (number): total Cashu token balance in satoshis
- `maxAutoPaySats` (number): per-payment safety cap
- `maxSpendPerMinuteSats` (number): rolling 60-second cap; 0 blocks auto-pay
- `maxSpendPerDaySats` (number): rolling 24-hour cap, persisted; 0 blocks auto-pay
- `spentLast24HoursSats` (number): automatic spend in the last 24 hours
- `credentialCount` (number): number of stored L402 credentials

LNURLcash notes are not reported here.

**When to use:** Call first in any session to understand what the agent can do autonomously.

---

### l402-discover

**Purpose:** Probe an endpoint to discover pricing without paying.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required): the endpoint to probe
- `method` (string, optional): HTTP method (default: GET)

**Returns:**
- `url` (string), `costSats` (number | null), `invoice` (string), `macaroon` (string), `paymentHash` (string)
- `server` (string): `"toll-booth"` when detected; absent otherwise
- `creditTiers` (array): credit tiers, present for toll-booth servers that offer them

The challenge is cached for a subsequent `l402-pay`. Only L402 challenges are read; any other response is an error.

**When to use:** Before committing to a purchase, so the agent can reason about value.

---

### l402-fetch

**Purpose:** Make an HTTP request with automatic L402 payment handling.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required): the endpoint to fetch
- `urls` (string[], optional): all transport URLs from `l402-search`, tried in preference order
- `pubkey` (string, optional): service pubkey from `l402-search`, used to share a credential across the service's transports
- `method` (string, optional): HTTP method (default: GET)
- `headers` (object, optional): additional headers
- `body` (string, optional): request body
- `autoPay` (boolean, optional, default false): pay a challenge within the limits
- `maxCostSats` (number, optional): most this call may pay; lowers `MAX_AUTO_PAY_SATS`, never raises it
- `txHash` (string, optional): transaction hash for the experimental x402 format
- `paymentFlow` (`"wildbloom-checkout-v1"`, optional): accepted only so that Wildbloom checkout can be refused; see the Wildbloom section

There is no payment-method argument; the payer is chosen as described under Wallet Priority and Resolution.

**Behaviour:**
1. Uses a stored credential only if it is bound to every origin the request may reach
2. Makes the HTTP request (with credential if available)
3. If 402 received and `autoPay` is set: refuses if an earlier payment to the service is unresolved, then checks the price against `MAX_AUTO_PAY_SATS`, `maxCostSats` and the rolling spend caps
4. If within the limits: pays, stores the credential bound to the request's origins, retries
5. Otherwise: returns the price and `paymentHash` unpaid, and caches the challenge for `l402-pay`
6. A payment whose outcome is unknown is reported as an error and recorded for `l402-reconcile`; it never falls through to another rail
7. Returns `status`, `headers`, `body` (in UNTRUSTED CONTENT markers), `creditsRemaining` and `satsPaid`, plus `paymentMethod` when an IETF Payment, LNURLcash or xCashu rail paid. An unpaid challenge returns `status: 402`, `costSats`, `invoice`, `paymentHash`, `creditsExhausted`, `tiers` when offered, and `message`. The human payer returns `paymentUrl` or a QR code and invoice instead

**When to use:** Primary tool for consuming L402 APIs. Handles the entire flow.

---

### l402-pay

**Purpose:** Pay a challenge that `l402-fetch` or `l402-discover` returned.

**Parameters:**
- `paymentHash` (string): payment hash of the cached challenge
- `invoice`, `macaroon` (string, optional): only for an invoice that did not come from a challenge; the human must approve it through MCP elicitation, or it is refused
- `method` (string, optional): `nwc`, `cashu`, `lnurlcash` or `human`

**Returns:**
- `paid` (boolean) and `paymentState` (`paid`, `failed`, `unknown` or `blocked`)
- `credentialsStored` (boolean)
- `method` (string): which wallet paid

For the human payer with a toll-booth payment page, polls that page for settlement for up to 120 seconds; with no payment page it polls the server's `/invoice-status/<hash>` endpoint for `HUMAN_PAY_TIMEOUT_S` seconds. Settlement can only be confirmed where the server reports it (toll-booth).

---

### l402-reconcile

**Purpose:** Resolve payments whose outcome is unknown.

**Parameters:**
- `paymentHash` (string, optional): omit to list unresolved payments
- `preimage` (string, optional): settles the payment if it hashes to `paymentHash`
- `abandon` (boolean, optional): stop tracking it; requires the human's approval through MCP elicitation

**Behaviour:** Asks the wallet that made the payment (NWC `lookup_invoice`, the Cashu mint for a reserved melt, or the LNURLcash verify URL). Settled with a matching preimage clears it and stores the L402 credential; definitely failed clears it and releases reserved Cashu proofs. While any is unresolved for a service, auto-pay to it is paused.

---

### l402-fetch-preview

**Purpose:** Show what an endpoint costs without paying. Its dependencies include no wallet or spend tracker, so it cannot spend. Widget hosts render the result as a payment confirmation dialog.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required), `urls` (string[], optional batch of up to 10)
- `method` (string, optional, default GET), `headers` (object, optional), `pubkey` (string, optional)

**Returns:** `status` (`preview`, `free` or `error`) with `endpoint`, `protocol`, `costSats` (`costUsd` for x402), `paymentMethod` (the wallet that would pay), `paymentHash`, `expiresAt` and `message`; an array when `urls` is given. It checks challenge types in the order IETF Payment, L402, LNURLcash, xCashu, x402, which differs from `l402-fetch`, so for a server sending several at once it may name a different rail.

---

### Widget tools

`l402-service-directory` (searchable service directory) and `l402-wallet-dashboard` (wallet status, limits, credentials) are MCP Apps widgets for hosts that support them.

---

### l402-credentials

**Purpose:** List all stored L402 credentials.

**Parameters:** None.

**Returns:** `credentials`, an array in which each entry has:
- `origin`: server origin, or the service pubkey the credential is keyed by when `l402-fetch` was given one
- `origins` (array, when recorded): the origins the credential was bought through and may be sent to
- `paymentHash`: payment hash of the purchase
- `creditBalance`: cached balance (if known)
- `server`: detected server type
- `storedAt` / `lastUsed`, timestamps

**When to use:** Auditing spend, checking which servers have been paid.

---

### l402-balance

**Purpose:** Check cached credit balance for a server.

**Parameters:**
- `origin` (string, required): server origin as a URL, e.g. `https://api.example.com`

**Returns:**
- `origin` (string)
- `creditsRemaining` (number | null): cached credits, or null if unknown
- `lastUpdated` (string): ISO timestamp of last use
- `stale` (boolean): true when older than 5 minutes

An error is returned if nothing is stored for that origin.

**When to use:** Before calling `l402-fetch` to confirm sufficient balance.

---

### l402-search

**Purpose:** Discover L402 services on Nostr relays.

**Parameters:**
- `query` (string, required): search text to match against service names, descriptions, capabilities
- `relays` (string[], optional): Nostr relay URLs (defaults to damus, primal, nos.lol)
- `topics` (string[], optional): filter by topic tags (e.g. ["ai", "data"])
- `paymentMethod` (string, optional): filter by payment rail, the first value of an announcement's `pmi` tag: `l402`, `cashu`, `xcashu`, `lnurlcash`, `x402` or `payment`
- `maxResults` (number, optional): max results (default 20)
- `timeout` (number, optional): relay timeout in ms (default 5000)

**Returns:** Array of services with:
- `name`, `urls` (array), `pubkey`, `about`, service metadata
- `pricing`: array of `{ capability, amount, unit }`
- `paymentMethods`: supported payment methods
- `topics`: topic tags
- `capabilities`: array of `{ name, description }` (optionally `endpoint`, `pricing`, `auth`, `timeout`)
- `storage`: present for storage services; see the Wildbloom section

Names, descriptions and capability text are wrapped in UNTRUSTED CONTENT markers. Topic filters are sent to the relays; the payment method and query text are matched locally, because relays index single-letter tags only.

**When to use:** When the agent needs a paid API but doesn't know the URL. Searches the decentralised Nostr network for kind 31402 service announcements. Services may advertise multiple transport URLs (clearnet, .onion, Handshake); pass the `urls` array and `pubkey` to `l402-fetch` for automatic transport selection and fallback.

---

### l402-store-token

**Purpose:** Store an L402 token obtained from a payment page, so later `l402-fetch` calls to that server are authenticated.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required): the service URL the token is for
- `token` (string, required): `macaroon:preimage`

**Returns:** `stored: true`, `origin` and `paymentHash` (when it can be read from the macaroon). A malformed macaroon or preimage is an error.

---

### l402-buy-credits (toll-booth only)

**Purpose:** Browse and purchase volume discount credit tiers.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required): toll-booth server URL
- `amountSats` (number, optional): specific tier to purchase
- `method` (string, optional): `nwc`, `cashu` or `human`

**Behaviour:** Fetches available tiers, purchases the specified tier, stores the credential with the credit balance.

**Returns:** without `amountSats`, `tiers`. After a purchase, `paid`, `amountSats`, `creditsReceived`, `credentialsStored` and `method`. The human payer returns a QR code with `invoice`, `paymentHash` and `costSats`; pay it, then call `l402-pay`.

**When to use:** When multiple requests are needed, buying a tier upfront is cheaper than paying per-request.

---

### l402-redeem-cashu (toll-booth only)

**Purpose:** Redeem Cashu ecash tokens directly with the server.

**Parameters:**
- `url` (string, required): toll-booth server URL
- `token` (string, required): Cashu token to redeem

**Behaviour:** Sends the raw Cashu token to the toll-booth's redemption endpoint. The server credits the balance immediately without a Lightning round-trip.

**Returns:** `redeemed: true`, `creditsReceived`, `credentialsStored`, and a `warning` if the credential could not be stored (the token is then kept for retry).

**When to use:** When both agent and server support Cashu, faster and cheaper than melting tokens to pay an invoice.

## L402 Protocol Flow

The L402 protocol is an extension of HTTP 402 (Payment Required):

1. **Client** sends a request to a protected endpoint
2. **Server** responds with `402 Payment Required` and headers:
   - `WWW-Authenticate: L402 macaroon="<base64>", invoice="<bolt11>"`
3. **Client** decodes the BOLT11 invoice, pays it via Lightning, receives a preimage
4. **Client** retries the request with:
   - `Authorization: L402 <base64-macaroon>:<hex-preimage>`
5. **Server** validates the macaroon + preimage and returns the data

402-mcp handles steps 2–5 automatically within `l402-fetch`.

## Supported 402 Protocol Variants

`l402-fetch` detects and handles four HTTP 402 challenge variants, plus an experimental x402 format. When a response carries several it checks them in this order and uses the first it can act on: LNURLcash, xCashu, x402, IETF Payment, L402. Every rail needs `autoPay: true` and a price within the limits.

| Protocol | Detection | Credential sent | Autonomous? |
|----------|-----------|----------------|-------------|
| **L402** | `WWW-Authenticate: L402 macaroon=…, invoice=…` | `Authorization: L402 <macaroon>:<preimage>` | Yes (any non-human payer) |
| **IETF Payment** (`draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01`) | `WWW-Authenticate: Payment id=… method=lightning …` | `Authorization: Payment <base64url-json>` | Yes (any non-human payer) |
| **LNURLcash** (LUD-25) | `X-LNURLcash: lnurlcashreq1<base64url>` | `X-LNURLcash: <bearer note URL>` | Yes (note store only) |
| **xCashu** (NUT-18) | `X-Cashu: creqA<base64url>` | `X-Cashu: <cashuB-token>` | Yes (Cashu wallet only) |
| **x402** (experimental, custom format) | `X-Payment-Required: x402` + JSON body | `X-Payment: <tx hash>` after the human pays | No: payment details shown to the human. Not the x402 specification, whose servers send a base64 `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header |

LNURLcash is checked before the others because a bearer note is already money in hand: the note URL goes straight into the retry header and the server settles it by rotating the note. If no note covers the price, or no note store is configured, the remaining challenges in the same response are tried. LNURLcash and xCashu are paid straight from their own stores and do not go through the payer order below. A note worth exactly the price is used as it is; otherwise one is split at the mint and the change stays in the store. The chosen note is held pending until the outcome is known, so nothing else can spend it in the meantime. xCashu uses coin selection via `wallet.send(amount, proofs, { includeFees: true })` and restores change proofs to the token store. IETF Payment decodes the base64url charge request to extract the BOLT11 invoice, then pays it through the payer order below and wraps the preimage in a JSON credential.

## Wallet Priority and Resolution

For a Lightning invoice (L402 and IETF Payment challenges, `l402-pay`, `l402-buy-credits`) the first available payer in this order is used: NWC, Cashu, LNURLcash, human. NWC is available when `NWC_URI_FILE` is set; Cashu and LNURLcash when their store holds a balance; the human payer is always available. One payer is chosen per payment and there is no fallback: if it fails, the failure is reported and the next payer is not tried.

| Wallet | Autonomy | Requirements | Speed |
|--------|----------|-------------|-------|
| NWC | Fully autonomous | `NWC_URI_FILE` pointing to a private 0600 bearer file | ~2-5 seconds |
| Cashu | Fully autonomous | `CASHU_TOKENS` file with ecash tokens | ~3-8 seconds |
| LNURLcash | Fully autonomous | `LNURLCASH_NOTES` file with LUD-25 bearer notes | ~2-6 seconds |
| Human | Requires human | None; always available, so it pays only when no other payer is available or `method: "human"` is passed | Minutes |

The agent can force a specific payer with the `method` parameter of `l402-pay` (`nwc`, `cashu`, `lnurlcash`, `human`) and `l402-buy-credits` (`nwc`, `cashu`, `human`). `l402-fetch` has no `method` parameter for payment. With the human payer, `l402-fetch` returns a payment page URL or a QR code at once instead of waiting; `l402-pay` then polls for settlement, which is only confirmed where the server reports it (toll-booth).

## Safety and Spend Limits

### Per-payment cap

`MAX_AUTO_PAY_SATS` (default: 1000) caps any single payment. A dearer challenge is not paid from any configured wallet, and the human wallet does not take over: the price and invoice go back to the agent, and whether it asks the human is up to the agent. `maxCostSats` on `l402-fetch` lowers the cap for one call. `0` disables auto-pay.

### Rolling spend cap

`MAX_SPEND_PER_MINUTE_SATS` (default: 10000) caps total spend in any 60-second window, and `MAX_SPEND_PER_DAY_SATS` (default: 5000) in any 24 hours; the daily window is kept in `~/.402-mcp/spend-ledger.json` so a restart does not reset it. `0` in either blocks auto-pay. At those defaults the daily cap is the lower one and spend in any minute also counts towards the day, so the per-minute cap never binds until you lower it or raise the daily cap. The budget set on the NWC connection is the real hard limit. These prevent:
- Rapid successive small payments exceeding a total budget
- Runaway loops where the agent keeps buying credits
- Both caps use atomic `tryRecord()` to prevent TOCTOU race conditions

### SSRF Protection

All outbound HTTP requests pass through an SSRF guard:
- Blocks requests to private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, ::1)
- Blocks requests to link-local, loopback, and metadata service IPs
- `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` disables this for local development only

### Credential Security

- Credentials encrypted with AES-256-GCM
- Encryption key stored in the OS keychain when available (macOS through the `security` command-line tool; elsewhere through the optional `keytar` module)
- Falls back to file-based key at `~/.402-mcp/encryption.key` with a console warning
- NWC capability and response events authenticated with NIP-44 v2 and signatures
- Returned NWC preimages verified against the challenged BOLT11 payment hash
- Preimages validated as hex before storage to prevent header injection
- Credential store path must be within the home directory (path traversal protection)

## Connecting an NWC Wallet

402-mcp needs Node.js 22.4 or newer. It reads the NWC connection URI from a private file, never from an environment variable. Create the file with owner-only permissions first and paste the URI into it with an editor, so the secret stays out of shell history:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.402-mcp
touch ~/.402-mcp/wallet.nwc
chmod 600 ~/.402-mcp/wallet.nwc
# open ~/.402-mcp/wallet.nwc in an editor, paste the URI on one line, save
claude mcp add 402-mcp -e NWC_URI_FILE="$HOME/.402-mcp/wallet.nwc" -- npx 402-mcp
```

The URI has the form `nostr+walletconnect://<wallet-pubkey-hex>?relay=<wss-relay-url>&secret=<secret-hex>`: a 64-character hex wallet pubkey and secret, one to eight `relay` values, an optional `lud16`, and no other parameters. The file must be a regular, non-empty file of at most 8192 bytes, and on macOS and Linux group and other must have no permissions. Create the connection with `pay_invoice` permission, a spending budget and NIP-44 v2 support; adding `lookup_invoice` lets `l402-reconcile` query the wallet. For Claude Desktop or Cursor, add an `env` block to the server entry with the absolute path of that file (JSON does not expand `~` or `$HOME`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "402-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["402-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "NWC_URI_FILE": "/absolute/path/to/.402-mcp/wallet.nwc",
        "MAX_AUTO_PAY_SATS": "1000"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A raw `NWC_URI` variable is refused at startup.

## Transport Modes

### stdio (default)

Standard MCP transport, used by Claude Desktop, Cursor, and most MCP clients. The server reads JSON-RPC from stdin and writes to stdout.

```bash
npx 402-mcp
```

### HTTP

StreamableHTTP transport, stateless. Prefer stdio wherever the client can start a local process: the HTTP transport can spend from the wallet.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.402-mcp && openssl rand -hex 32 > ~/.402-mcp/http.token && chmod 600 ~/.402-mcp/http.token
TRANSPORT=http HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE=~/.402-mcp/http.token PORT=3402 npx 402-mcp
```

HTTP transport includes:
- Bearer token required on every request (`HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE`, a private 0600 file); the server refuses to start in http mode without one
- DNS rebinding protection: only requests whose `Host` header is a loopback name with the port, the bound address, or listed in `HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` are answered
- Rate limiting: 100 requests per 60 seconds per IP
- Security headers: CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Cache-Control
- Loopback-only binding by default (`BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1`)
- Health endpoint at `GET /health`
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT

## Configuration Reference

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `NWC_URI_FILE` | - | Path to a private 0600 file containing the NWC bearer URI. Raw NWC_URI is refused. |
| `CASHU_TOKENS` | - | Path to Cashu token store file. Must be within home directory. |
| `LNURLCASH_NOTES` | - | Path to LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer note store file. Must be within home directory. |
| `MAX_AUTO_PAY_SATS` | 1000 | Per-payment safety cap (satoshis). 0 disables autonomous payments. |
| `MAX_SPEND_PER_MINUTE_SATS` | 10000 | Rolling 60-second spend cap (satoshis). 0 blocks auto-pay. |
| `MAX_SPEND_PER_DAY_SATS` | 5000 | Rolling 24-hour spend cap (satoshis), persisted across restarts. 0 blocks auto-pay. |
| `CREDENTIAL_STORE` | `~/.402-mcp/credentials.json` | Path to encrypted credential store. Must be within home directory. |
| `TRANSPORT` | `stdio` | Transport mode: `stdio` or `http`. |
| `PORT` | 3402 | HTTP server port (when `TRANSPORT=http`). |
| `BIND_ADDRESS` | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address. Warning emitted for non-loopback addresses. |
| `HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` | - | Private 0600 file holding the bearer token (32+ characters). Required when `TRANSPORT=http`. Raw HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN is refused. |
| `HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | - | Extra `Host` header values to accept (comma-separated), e.g. a reverse proxy's name. |
| `CORS_ORIGIN` | disabled | CORS origin for HTTP transport (`*` or one origin). `*` logs a warning. |
| `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | 30000 | HTTP request timeout in milliseconds. |
| `FETCH_MAX_RETRIES` | 2 | Maximum retry attempts for failed requests. Money-mutating POSTs use 0. |
| `FETCH_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` | 10485760 | Maximum response body size (10 MB). |
| `HUMAN_PAY_TIMEOUT_S` | 600 | How long the human payer polls for settlement (seconds) when there is no payment page to poll. |
| `HUMAN_PAY_POLL_S` | 3 | Initial polling interval for human payment (seconds). |
| `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | false | Allow requests to private IP ranges. Local development only. |
| `ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS` | false | Acknowledge the risk when `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` is set. |
| `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` | - | If set to "0" (disables TLS validation), 402-mcp refuses to start unless `ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` or `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true`; with either it starts and logs a warning. |
| `TRANSPORT_PREFERENCE` | `onion,hns,https,http` | Preferred transport order for multi-URL services. |
| `TOR_PROXY` | - | SOCKS5 proxy for .onion requests only (e.g. `socks5h://127.0.0.1:9050`). |
| `SOCKS_PROXY` | - | SOCKS5 proxy for every paid-API request, names resolved by the proxy. Set this or `TOR_PROXY`, not both. Wallet and relay traffic is not proxied. |
| `HNS_GATEWAY_URL` | `https://query.hdns.io/` | DNS-over-HTTPS resolver for Handshake (HNS) names. Any host name ordinary DNS cannot find is sent here. |

## Multi-Transport Endpoints

Services discovered via `l402-search` may advertise multiple transport URLs for censorship resistance. If a DNS seizure, registrar suspension, or CA revocation takes down one endpoint, the agent automatically falls back to an alternative.

### Transport Types

| Transport | Example | Detection |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| Onion | `http://abc123...onion/api` | Hostname ends in `.onion` |
| Handshake | `https://api.myservice.hns/api` | TLD is `.hns`. A TLD that is neither on the built-in list of common ICANN TLDs nor `.hns` (such as `.pub`) is a guessed Handshake name and ranks after the later of `hns` and `https` |
| HTTPS | `https://api.example.com/api` | Standard TLD + `https://` |
| HTTP | `http://api.example.com/api` | Standard TLD + `http://` |

### Selection and Fallback

1. **Filter**: .onion URLs are removed when no Tor proxy is configured
2. **Sort**: URLs are ordered by `TRANSPORT_PREFERENCE` (default: onion > hns > https > http); the values are `onion`, `hns`, `https` and `http`. A guessed Handshake name is placed just after whichever of `hns` and `https` is later in the list, and last if `hns` is not listed
3. **Try**: each URL is tried in order; connection-level failures (DNS, ECONNREFUSED, timeout, TLS failure) trigger fallback to the next URL
4. **Stop**: any HTTP response (including 402, 500) is returned immediately without fallback

### HNS Resolution

Handshake names are resolved via DNS-over-HTTPS (RFC 8484 wire format) through the configured gateway. When standard DNS returns NXDOMAIN, the SSRF guard tries HNS resolution as a fallback. Resolved IPs are validated against blocked ranges before connecting. `HNS_GATEWAY_URL` has a default (`https://query.hdns.io/`), so Handshake endpoints need no configuration. Under `SOCKS_PROXY` Handshake lookups are switched off, because the DNS-over-HTTPS query would go around the proxy; the proxy resolves every name instead.

### Credential Portability

When `l402-fetch` is given a service **pubkey** (from the kind 31402 event, as returned by `l402-search`), the credential is keyed by it; without one it is keyed by origin. Either way it is bound to the transport origins it was bought through. A macaroon obtained via a Tor hidden service works over the service's clearnet URL, and vice versa, when both were in the `urls` list at purchase. A credential is never sent to an origin it is not bound to, whatever pubkey the request names.

## Ecosystem

| Project | Role | URL |
|---------|------|-----|
| **402-mcp** | MCP client, AI agents discover, pay, and consume L402 APIs | https://github.com/forgesworn/402-mcp |
| **toll-booth** | L402 payment middleware for any Node.js server | https://github.com/forgesworn/toll-booth |
| **satgate** | Pay-per-token AI inference proxy (built on toll-booth) | https://github.com/TheCryptoDonkey/satgate |
| **402-announce** | Publish L402 services on Nostr for decentralised discovery | https://github.com/forgesworn/402-announce |

## Integration Patterns

### Agent discovers and consumes a paid API

```
1. l402-config()                    → Understand capabilities
2. l402-search("routing")           → Find services on Nostr
3. l402-discover(service_url)       → Check pricing
4. l402-fetch(service_url, autoPay)  → Pay (within the limits) and consume
```

### Agent buys credits for repeated access

```
1. l402-discover(url)               → Detect toll-booth, check tiers
2. l402-buy-credits(url, 500)       → Buy 500-sat tier (555 credits)
3. l402-fetch(url, ...) × N         → Use credits (the stored credential is sent; no autoPay needed)
4. l402-balance(url)                → Check remaining credits
```

### Agent redeems Cashu tokens directly

```
1. l402-discover(url)               → Confirm toll-booth server
2. l402-redeem-cashu(url, token)    → Direct ecash redemption
3. l402-fetch(url, ...)             → Use credits from redemption
```

### Agent discovers service with transport fallback

```
1. l402-search("weather data")       → Service found with 3 URLs (clearnet, .onion, HNS)
2. l402-fetch(urls, pubkey: ...)     → Tries .onion first (if Tor configured)
                                       → .onion down? Falls back to HNS
                                       → HNS unreachable? Falls back to clearnet
3. l402-balance(url)                 → Credential works across all transports (keyed by pubkey)
```

### Agent with no wallet (human-in-the-loop)

```
1. l402-fetch(url, autoPay)        → 402 received; payment page URL or QR shown
2. Human pays via wallet app
3. l402-pay(paymentHash)            → polls the toll-booth payment page, stores the credential
4. l402-fetch(url)                  → data returned

Settlement can only be confirmed where the server reports it (toll-booth).
```

## Storage service announcements (Wildbloom)

`l402-search` also returns storage services announced with the `forgesworn-storage-service-v1` profile (kind 31402, validated by `402-announce/storage` 2.3.0). Wildbloom is one such service: it offers paid storage, and a free tier called free shelter, which keeps copies pushed by authorised mirrors on a best-effort basis, may evict them, and does not take direct uploads from unknown users.

These results are descriptive only. A paid storage result carries `storage.paymentFlow: "wildbloom-checkout-v1"` and `autoPaySupported: false`, and 402-mcp cannot buy it. Do not hand that flow to `l402-fetch` or `l402-pay`: both refuse it, and `l402-fetch` also refuses any `/checkout/v1` path, before any network, credential or wallet access. To buy, read the operator's current terms (its `/services/v1` listing) and use Wildbloom's own checkout, which asks for a private quote signed with NIP-98 (Nostr HTTP authentication) and an explicit payment from you. Mirroring to free shelter is not something these tools do either. The terms in an announcement are the operator's own claims, not a recommendation or proof of uptime, and a valid signature shows only who published it; it never authorises a purchase.

How results are chosen: search contacts only the relays you name (or the defaults), never a storage node or a wallet. The newest valid signed announcement for each service (same publisher and `d` tag; on equal timestamps the lowest event ID) is selected before expiry, withdrawal and query filters apply. So that a relay replaying an older copy cannot revive a withdrawn or expired offer, the newest record seen for each service is kept in memory as a watermark: up to 2,000 per search handler, kept across calls until the server restarts, and a search that would exceed that fails with an error rather than dropping any. A fresh server has no watermarks, so it cannot know about a record a relay leaves out. Full or paused listings that are still current remain in the results; expired and withdrawn ones stay as watermarks but are not returned. Discovery stores nothing on disk and opens no browser.

## Using the modules in code

The package exposes nine subpath imports, each mapping to `build/<path>.js` with its declaration file beside it: `402-mcp/tools/*`, `402-mcp/l402/*`, `402-mcp/x402/*`, `402-mcp/xcashu/*`, `402-mcp/xlnurlcash/*`, `402-mcp/ietf-payment/*`, `402-mcp/store/*`, `402-mcp/fetch/*` and `402-mcp/spend-tracker`. These are the server's own modules, exposed as they are; read `src/` for signatures. Do not import the package root (`402-mcp`) from library code: `main` and the `.` export both point at the server entry, `build/index.js`, which loads configuration from the environment and connects a transport as soon as it is imported.

```ts
import { SpendTracker } from '402-mcp/spend-tracker'
import { parseL402Challenge } from '402-mcp/l402/parse'

const tracker = new SpendTracker()
console.log(tracker.tryRecord(50, 10_000)) // true: 50 sats fits under a 10,000 sat per-minute cap

const challenge = parseL402Challenge('L402 macaroon="AgEEbG5kcg==", invoice="lnbc10n1pexample"')
console.log(challenge) // { macaroon: 'AgEEbG5kcg==', invoice: 'lnbc10n1pexample' }
```
